title: Australia has no licensing regime, construction supply chain or operating workforce for nuclear power reactors
oneLiner: The national regulator licenses research reactors and medical facilities, not power plants.
body: The Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency regulates one research reactor at Lucas Heights and radiation use in medicine and industry. It has no framework for licensing, inspecting or decommissioning a power reactor, and no Australian firm has built one. Each of these would have to be created before construction could begin.
contextBackground: Australia has operated research reactors since 1958 and has a mature radiation-safety profession. What it has never had is the much larger regulatory, engineering and training apparatus that power reactors require, which in other countries took a decade or more to establish.
contextDisagreement: Nobody disputes the gap. The argument is about how long it takes to close: whether regulatory frameworks can be adopted from the United States or Canada largely as-is, or must be built from first principles.

evidenceItems.citation: Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency — regulatory functions and licensed facilities

otherClaim.title: A first Australian nuclear power reactor could not be generating electricity before 2040

claimItself.title: A first Australian nuclear power reactor could not be generating electricity before 2040
claimItself.oneLiner: Legislation, licensing, site selection, workforce and construction each take years, and none has started.
claimItself.body: Starting from no regulator for power reactors, no licensed site and no construction supply chain, the sequence of repeal, regulatory design, licensing, approvals and a first-of-a-kind build is estimated by CSIRO and others at fifteen years or more. On that reckoning a decision taken now delivers first power around 2040 at the earliest.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Australia has no licensing regime, construction supply chain or operating workforce for nuclear power reactors

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: The United Arab Emirates went from deciding to build nuclear power to first grid electricity in about twelve years, with no prior nuclear industry

ownArguments.label: FOR
